title: The Lion and the Mouse
source: Aesop's Fables (public domain), gently retold for bedtime

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Once upon a time, at the edge of a quiet forest, where the tall grass turned gold in the evening light...

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: there lived a great lion. He was big, and strong, and his mane was as warm as the setting sun.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And on this soft, sleepy evening, the lion lay beneath his favourite old tree... fast asleep.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Not far away, a tiny mouse was hurrying home. Pitter, patter, pitter, patter, went her little feet.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She was in such a rush, that she did not look where she was going... and she ran right over the lion's nose!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The lion opened one big golden eye. And, very gently, he placed his paw on the end of her tail.

lines.speaker: lion
lines.text: Well, well, well... Who is this? Tickling my nose, and waking me from my lovely dream?

lines.speaker: mouse
lines.text: Oh! I'm so sorry, Mister Lion! I didn't mean to wake you. I was only hurrying home.

lines.speaker: mouse
lines.text: Please, let me go. And maybe, one day, I can help you, too.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The lion began to chuckle. A deep, rumbly chuckle, like far away thunder.

lines.speaker: lion
lines.text: Ho, ho! You? Help me? Oh, but you are so very small, little one.

lines.speaker: lion
lines.text: Still... you made me smile. Off you go, then. Hurry home... and sleep well.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And he lifted his paw, and let the little mouse go.

lines.speaker: mouse
lines.text: Thank you! Thank you, kind lion! I will never forget it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The mouse scampered away into the grass, and the stars came out, one by one, over the quiet forest.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Days went by. The moon grew round, and then thin, and then round again.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then, one evening, the lion went walking through the forest, looking for a cool place to rest.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But hidden among the leaves, was a great net of ropes, that some hunters had left behind.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Swish! The net fell down around him. The lion pulled, and pushed, and wriggled... but the ropes held him tight.

lines.speaker: lion
lines.text: Oh dear... oh dear me. I cannot get free.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So the lion lifted his head, and gave a long, low roar, that rolled across the whole forest.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Far away, in her cosy little home, the mouse heard the roar. And she knew that voice at once.

lines.speaker: mouse
lines.text: That's my friend, the lion! He needs me. I'm coming!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Pitter, patter, pitter, patter. She ran through the grass, and over the roots, and under the ferns, as fast as her little feet could carry her.

lines.speaker: mouse
lines.text: Don't worry, Mister Lion. Stay very still. I know just what to do.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And with her tiny, sharp teeth, the mouse began to nibble at the ropes. Nibble, nibble, nibble.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One rope snapped. Then another. And another. Until, at last, the whole net fell away, and the lion was free.

lines.speaker: lion
lines.text: Little mouse... you saved me! I laughed, when you said you could help me. But you were right.

lines.speaker: mouse
lines.text: You were kind to me, when I was small and scared. So now, I was kind to you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And from that day on, the great lion and the tiny mouse were the very best of friends.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Sometimes, on warm summer nights, you could find them together, under the old tree, watching the fireflies glow.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Because no act of kindness, no matter how small, is ever wasted. And even the littlest friend, can do the biggest things.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Now the lion is yawning, and the mouse is curled up warm, right inside his soft, golden mane.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The stars are twinkling. The forest is quiet. And it's time for you to close your eyes, too.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Goodnight, little one. Sweet dreams.
